raw_segments.text: All the kingdoms that Augustus gained by the right of war, he either restored to those who had lost them or presented them to strangers.
And Tacitus, in reference to this, speaking of Cogidunus, king of England, gives us, by a marvellous touch, an instance of that infinite power.
The Romans, says he, were from all antiquity accustomed to leave the kings they had subdued in possession of their kingdoms under their authority.
